component.name: Gaia Sky
component.developer_name: Zentrum für Astronomie der Universität Heidelberg

description.p: Gaia Sky is an astronomy visualization platform for desktop and VR that runs on Linux, Windows and macOS. It is developed in the framework of ESA's Gaia mission to chart about 1 billion stars of our Galaxy in the Gaia group of the Astronomisches Rechen-Institut (ZAH, Universität Heidelberg). Explore the Solar System, the Milky Way, and even the most distant galaxies of our Universe with up-to-date, real scientific data.

This is a major release, accompanying the Gaia DR4 data release. It adds new DR4-based datasets, three-dimensional galaxies and clouds, new light shafts and particle effects, smoother camera motion, and many bug fixes.

ul.li: New datasets based on Gaia DR4.
Galaxies from the procedural generator can be rendered as real 3D volumes of gas, dust and stars, with dust lanes that hide what is behind them.
Atmospheres are no longer blended additively: a lit daytime sky now properly hides the stars and the Milky Way, the Sun stays visible, and eclipses dim the sky.
New light shafts (god rays) around the Sun and nearby stars, replacing the old light scattering effect.
Motion particle effects are reimplemented, and nearby stars are drawn by a single consistent method.
Camera speed follows a smooth curve across the whole range of distances, and is no longer held back by faded-out objects.
Scene files can orient bodies by their IAU rotation pole and declare the reference plane of orbital elements (JPL conventions), plus a new inheritOpacity setting.
Fixes for planet shadows, instanced-set draw counts, orbits of TLE satellites, octree datasets, and volumes at large distance scales.

description.p: This is a bug-fix release. The procedural galaxy is drawn at the right size and position, the background grid annotations are back, and a camera teleport when focusing large objects is fixed.

ul.li: Procedural galaxy volumes are drawn at the correct size and position (they were 5% too large and off-centre). Volumes generated with an older particles-to-volume.py must be regenerated.
Volume labels are no longer 10 times too large.
The latitude/longitude annotations of the equatorial, ecliptic and galactic grids are visible again.
Fixed-function GL state no longer leaks between render groups, and render-group teardown no longer skips state restoration on failure.
Focusing an object that opts out of camera collision (e.g. the Milky Way) no longer teleports the camera out of it.
Focus resolution no longer jumps to the first particle of a set when a name is not in its index.
The galaxy volume is 1.37 times larger, giving a 17 kpc gas disk with the Sun at 0.47 of it, and dust scattering is enabled.
